modes.name: playInView
modes.behavior: on first intersection while scrolling DOWN, setMode('forward') and play(); if playReverse and the user then scrolls UP back into view, setMode('reverse') and play(). Scroll direction is tracked by a shared rAF-batched scroll listener.

modes.name: playScrollMidline
modes.behavior: compares the viewport midline to the element: `r = (innerHeight/2 - rect.top) / rect.height`. r ≥ 0.5 → play forward to the end; r < 0.5 → play reverse to frame 0. Re-evaluated on every scroll frame and after each 'complete' event.

modes.name: playScrollScrub
modes.behavior: frame is scrubbed directly from scroll position: `start = innerHeight - 0.5*height`, `end = -height`, raw = clamp((start - rect.top)/(start-end)); the first observed raw is stored as a baseline c and the played range is remapped to (raw - c)/(1 - c); frame = t * (totalFrames - 1) via setFrame(). renderConfig gets `freezeOnOffscreen:false`.

patterns.scrollBatching: one shared `scroll` (passive) and one shared `resize` listener with a single requestAnimationFrame per frame, fanned out to all subscribed players

every `h-(--vp-height)` sticky stage tracks the real visual viewport, so mobile browser chrome appearing/disappearing does not break the pinned sections

theFiveRules: Pick TWO easing curves and use them for 90% of everything: cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) for entrances, cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1) for UI state. Add cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1) only for long crossfades and reveals.
Entrances are SLOW (0.9–2s) and state changes are FAST (0.09–0.3s). There is nothing in the 0.4–0.8s band except hover transforms. That gap is what makes it feel considered rather than busy.

Scroll-linked motion is always a small, bounded range fed through a slightly-overdamped spring (stiffness 200–320, damping 28–34, mass 0.35–0.45). Never raw scroll for anything the eye tracks; raw scroll only for parallax and pin offsets.
Hover scale is 1.02–1.06, never more. Buttons use 1.0375. The motion is in colour and in the icon slide, not in size.

Every big reveal gets ONE companion beat on a delay: the highlight sweep then the card at 1.75s; the stat number then the 1.2s rule; the typewriter then the italic flip at 450ms. One follow-through, never two.
